# Hasher

A hash being computed, one write at a time.

```rux
pub interface Hasher {
    func Write(self: &var Self, bytes: *byte, length: uint);
    func Finish(self: &var Self) -> uint64;
}
```

Written as an interface so a generic can require it. Borrow an implementation under a bound so mutations apply
to the caller's state without copying it.
An implementation must give the same answer for the same sequence of bytes, whatever the writes were split into:
writing eight bytes at once and writing them one at a time must agree. It must not read anything but the bytes it
is given — no address, no counter, no clock.

## Requirements

<h3 id="write"><code>Write</code></h3>

```rux
func Write(self: &var Self, bytes: *byte, length: uint)
```

Adds `length` bytes at `bytes` to what is being hashed.
`bytes` is borrowed and read; `length` is read by value. A zero length is legal and changes nothing, and is
the one case in which `bytes` may be null.
Runs in time proportional to `length` and allocates nothing.
`bytes` must be readable for `length` bytes.

| Name     | Type    | Description                          |
| -------- | ------- | ------------------------------------ |
| `bytes`  | `*byte` | the bytes to absorb                  |
| `length` | `uint`  | how many bytes; zero absorbs nothing |

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Hash/Src/Hasher.rux#L27)

<h3 id="finish"><code>Finish</code></h3>

```rux
func Finish(self: &var Self) -> uint64
```

The hash of everything written so far.
Returns the answer by value and leaves the hasher usable: asking twice gives the same answer, and writing
more afterwards continues from where the writes left off rather than starting over.
Cannot fail. Runs in constant time and allocates nothing.

**Returns**: the hash of everything written since the last reset

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Hash/Src/Hasher.rux#L35)

## Related

<h3 id="hash-bytes"><code>HashBytes&lt;H&gt;</code></h3>

```rux
pub func HashBytes<H: Hasher>(
    hasher: &var H,
    bytes: *byte,
    length: uint
) -> uint64
```

Writes `length` bytes and returns the hash, for a caller with nothing else to add.
`hasher` is borrowed mutably and left holding what it hashed; `bytes` is borrowed and read. The type argument
must be written out — `HashBytes<Fnv1a64>(hasher, data, length)` — because a generic argument is never
inferred.
Cannot fail. Runs in time proportional to `length` and allocates nothing.
`bytes` must be readable for `length` bytes.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Hash/Src/Hasher.rux#L50)

<h3 id="write-byte"><code>WriteByte&lt;H&gt;</code></h3>

Writes one byte into `hasher`.
`hasher` is borrowed mutably; `value` is read by value.
Cannot fail. Runs in constant time and allocates nothing.

<h3 id="write-uint32"><code>WriteUint32&lt;H&gt;</code></h3>

```rux
pub func WriteUint32<H: Hasher>(
    hasher: &var H,
    value: uint32
)
```

Writes a 32-bit value into `hasher`, least significant byte first.
`hasher` is borrowed mutably; `value` is read by value. The byte order is fixed rather than the machine's, so a
value hashes the same on every target — which is what makes a hash of a struct mean the same thing everywhere.
Cannot fail. Runs in constant time and allocates nothing.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Hash/Src/Hasher.rux#L75)

| -------- | -------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| `hasher` | `&var H` | the hasher to write to                    |
| `value`  | `uint32` | the value, written as little-endian bytes |

Writes a 64-bit value into `hasher`, least significant byte first.
`hasher` is borrowed mutably; `value` is read by value. The byte order is fixed rather than the machine's, for
the same reason as [`WriteUint32`](/docs/api/hash/hasher#write-uint32).
Cannot fail. Runs in constant time and allocates nothing.
